free_tier.stated: Up to 10 GB free - 3-day link expiration
free_tier.notes: Paid tiers go to 5 TB per transfer; the free tier is the 10 GB row.

per_object_cap.stated: Up to 10 GB free, or up to 5 TB with a paid transfer
per_object_cap.notes: Decimal GB as written on the page; the boundary was not pushed to.

egress.terms: The page advertises no per-download charge and no account; traffic is not metered on the free tier as stated.

interface_detail: A browser drop zone. No anonymous HTTP upload endpoint was found: POST to /api/upload, /upload, /api/files and /v1/upload all returned 403 from the edge, so the upload is a browser-orchestrated presigned flow whose endpoint is inside a JS bundle.
tooling: Browser only as observed. A wrapper would need a headless browser or the presigned-URL flow read out of the JS bundle; neither was done here.
chaining: A 10 GB drop with a 3-day life is the hand-off tier: send a finished archive to one reader, not a mirror an archive can be rebuilt from.
limits_note: Four shape probes at the likely API paths returned 403 rather than 404, so the edge is refusing before the application sees the request.
binding_note: 10 GB per transfer with a 3-day life: at 1 TiB a month the object size forces 100 transfers, and the retention means none of them is still there when the month ends.

identity_cost.detail: The page states no account is needed for the free 10 GB tier; uploads are browser-driven and no registration was attempted.

reliability_note: An SEO-visible 2026 entrant with no published API and an edge that refuses unknown POSTs; nothing indicates long-term operation.
confidence_note: The offer and the 3-day expiry are quoted from the vendor page read today; the upload path could not be driven from a script, so no byte was moved and the cap is the vendor's sentence only.

evidence.proved: 'Up to 10 GB free - 3-day link expiration' and 'Share up to 10 GB free - or up to 5 TB'
multipart POST to /api/upload, /upload, /api/files, /v1/upload, /api/v1/upload -> HTTP 403 on all five, so no anonymous HTTP upload endpoint is exposed

notes: that is a tooling note, not a rejection.
